question: In which period is the first inscriptional example of the practice of Sati found?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gupta.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first inscriptional **example of the **practice of Sati **is found in the **Gupta period.**
 
• **Sati** was a practice where a **widow **would immolate herself on her** husband's funeral pyre.**
 
• The **Gupta period** was known for its cultural and artistic achievements, as well as its **promotion of Hinduism.**
 
• The **Maukhari and Vardhana dynasties** were both North Indian dynasties that preceded the Gupta dynasty.
 
• The** Satavahana dynasty** was a South Indian dynasty that existed before the Gupta period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Evangelists like **Carey** and Hindu reformers like **Ram Mohan Roy **opposed the practice of sati, which finally prompted British Governor-General of India **Lord William Bentinck** to implement the** Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.**
 
• It stated that Hindu widows who are **burned or buried alive** will face legal action from the **criminal courts.**
 
• Subsequent laws were passed to combat what the British believed to be connected problems concerning** violence against Hindu women**.
 
• These laws included the **Age of Consent Act of 1891,** the **Female Infanticide Prevention Act of 1870**, and the** Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856.**
 
• Sati is defined as the **act or rite **itself in **Part I, Section 2(c) **of the Indian Commission of **Sati (Prevention) Act, 1987**.
